title: Efficacy and Safety of Intraosseous Regional Versus Intravenous Tranexamic Acid in Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Tranexamic acid (TXA) reduces perioperative blood loss in total knee arthroplasty (TKA); however, evidence for intraosseous regional administration (IORA) remains limited. We evaluated the efficacy and safety of IORA-TXA versus intravenous TXA (IV-TXA) in TKA. METHODS: In this prospective, randomized, single-center trial, 98 patients undergoing primary TKA were randomized 1:1 to IORA-TXA or IV-TXA (49 per group) at a uniform dose of 20 mg/kg. The primary outcome was calculated perioperative blood loss. Secondary efficacy outcomes included calculated hidden blood loss, postoperative hemoglobin (Hb) levels, and transfusion rate. Safety outcomes included deep vein thrombosis (DVT), muscular calf vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism (PE), and wound-related complications. RESULTS: Compared with IV-TXA, IORA-TXA reduced calculated perioperative blood loss (674.8 ± 335.0 vs. 817.5 ± 357.2 mL; mean difference, 142.6 mL; 95% CI, 7.4-277.8; p = 0.038) and calculated hidden blood loss (644.8 ± 335.5 vs. 790.9 ± 339.0 mL; mean difference, 146.1 mL; 95% CI, 10.9-281.3; p = 0.035). Postoperative Hb was similar on POD1 (134.0 ± 9.8 vs. 130.1 ± 11.1 g/L; p = 0.067) but was higher with IORA-TXA on POD2 (119.8 ± 8.3 vs. 113.8 ± 11.5 g/L; mean difference 6.0 g/L; 95% CI 2.0-10.0; p = 0.005) and POD3 (114.8 ± 7.9 vs. 109.8 ± 12.6 g/L; mean difference 5.0 g/L; 95% CI 0.8-9.2; p = 0.020). No patient required blood transfusion. DVT detected by routine postoperative Doppler occurred numerically more often with IORA-TXA than with IV-TXA: 10.2% (95% CI, 3.4%-22.2%) versus 0.0% (95% CI, 0.0%-7.3%); p = 0.056. CONCLUSIONS: IORA-TXA reduced calculated perioperative and hidden blood loss and improved early postoperative Hb preservation compared with IV-TXA. However, DVT incidence was numerically higher with IORA-TXA, indicating a potential thromboembolic safety signal that warrants confirmation in larger, adequately powered trials. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Therapeutic Level I. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

title: Lower-extremity Deep Vein Thrombosis after Plastic Surgery: Clinical Characteristics and Outcomes in a Retrospective Case Series.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a significant complication in plastic surgery, particularly affecting the lower extremities. Understanding the associated characteristics can aid in developing effective prevention strategies. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, quality improvement-oriented case series of 5 ultrasound-confirmed symptomatic postoperative lower-extremity DVT events after plastic surgery under general anesthesia at a single institution (January 2020-May 2024). Among 39,055 general anesthesia procedures during the study period, de-identified records were reviewed for patient and procedural characteristics, prophylaxis and mobility pathways, duplex ultrasonography confirmation, management, and short-term outcomes. No non-DVT comparator cohort was extracted; analyses were descriptive and not intended for risk-factor inference. One patient with postoperative chest/back pain and transfer for suspected pulmonary embolism without in-hospital lower-extremity DVT confirmation was excluded from the final case series. RESULTS: The 5 included cases were clinically heterogeneous and involved complex perioperative settings, including post-massive weight loss body contouring, craniofacial reconstruction with implant use, neurosurgical-related reconstruction, extensive head and neck lesion surgery, and posttraumatic facial reconstruction. All DVTs were confirmed by duplex Doppler ultrasonography, with thrombi involving the posterior tibial, peroneal, or calf muscular veins. Several cases involved prolonged procedures, reoperation for postoperative hematoma, or delayed mobilization. Postoperative anticoagulation was administered in most cases, whereas postoperative mechanical prophylaxis was not consistently documented. CONCLUSIONS: In a very low-frequency setting, this series highlights potentially actionable prevention gaps-especially postoperative mechanical prophylaxis and mobility disruptions-rather than establishing causal risk factors.

title: Epidemiological Characteristics of Venous Thromboembolism and Associated Indicators for Catheter-Related Thrombosis Subtypes.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a severe and life-threatening complication in hospitalized patients, and central venous catheter (CVC) insertion significantly increases the risk of catheter-related thrombosis (CRT). Epidemiological profiles of hospitalized patients with confirmed VTE are characterized; indicators correlated with CRT subtype are identified; the discriminative performance of circulating biomarkers is evaluated; and VTE recurrence metrics are contrasted between cohorts with and without CVC placement. A single-center retrospective case-case comparative analysis is conducted on 862 patients with imaging-confirmed VTE. Analytical methodologies incorporate univariate and multivariate logistic regression, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve testing. The in-hospital VTE incidence was 2.1%, concentrated in elderly, malignancy, and postoperative patients. CRT incidence was 10.2%, highest with peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC). Five clinical indicators correlated with CRT subtype were identified: prolonged catheter indwelling, catheter malposition, elevated D-dimer levels, malignant tumor history, and prior VTE events. The combination of D-dimer and catheter indwelling time exhibited robust discriminative power (AUC = 0.82) for differentiating CRT from non-CRT VTE among patients with confirmed VTE. The 6-month VTE recurrence rate was 28.4% in the CVC group and 9.7% in the non-CVC group. These observational findings yield only tentative clinical hypotheses aimed at distinguishing thrombotic subtypes among VTE patients. Further multicenter prospective research is necessary to validate these indicators and develop mature, standardized prevention protocols for broad clinical application.

title: Endovascular Therapy for Femoropopliteal Artery Lesions Involving the Popliteal Artery: 1-Year Outcomes from a Real-World Multicenter Registry.
abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate real-world outcomes of endovascular treatment for femoropopliteal lesions involving the popliteal artery and, in a post-hoc exploratory analysis, assess whether anatomical location (P3 vs. P1/P2 segments) was associated with clinical decision-making and prognosis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, post-hoc analysis of 946 patients from the prospective PROMISING registry. For this exploratory analysis, patients were stratified according to distal (P3) versus proximal/mid (P1/P2) popliteal artery involvement. Predictors of stent implantation and clinical decision pathways were compared across groups. RESULTS: Overall procedural success was 98.5%, and the 12-month freedom from major adverse events (MAE), defined as a composite of all-cause mortality, major amputation, or clinically driven target lesion revascularization, was 80.1%. Multivariable analysis indicated P3 involvement independently predicted reduced stent implantation (OR 0.66, 95% CI 0.46-0.95, p = 0.027). For vessel preparation, the P3 group more frequently utilized plain old balloon angioplasty (POBA, 67.8% vs. 54.8%, p < 0.001) rather than directional atherectomy or specialty balloons. Despite a lower stent implantation rate and greater use of POBA, 12-month freedom from MAE was comparable between the P3 and P1/P2 groups (78.0% vs. 81.2%, p = 0.481). CONCLUSION: In this post-hoc analysis of real-world registry data, popliteal lesion location was associated with differences in operator treatment strategies. P3 involvement was associated with less frequent stent implantation and greater use of plain balloon angioplasty, while 1-year clinical outcomes were comparable between the P3 and P1/P2 groups. These exploratory findings require external validation before they can be used to inform clinical treatment strategies. title: Imaging And Outcomes In The Treatment Of Sacral Dural Arteriovenous Fistulas.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Spinal dural arteriovenous fistulas (DAVFs) in the sacral region are extremely rare and their intradural retrograde draining system has not been investigated in detail. The aim of this study was to characterize the venous drainage patterns of sacral DAVFs based on our clinical experience in treating patients with this condition. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed the clinical data of patients with sacral DAVFs treated at our institution from January 2016 to January 2024. Preoperative spinal angiography was used to evaluate the positional relationship between the shunt point of sacral DAVF and the vertebral midline. We proposed that if the location of the shunt point was located on the midline, the draining vein would be the filum terminale vein (FTV); if the shunt point was located off the midline, the draining vein would be the radiculomedullary vein (RMV). RESULTS: A total of 17 sacral DAVFs patients treated with direct surgery were included in this study. All patients presented with lower extremity weakness and numbness. Sphincter dysfunction was present in 15 patients (88.2%). The mean interval from symptom onset to diagnosis was 14.1 months (range 1-96 months). Preoperative magnetic resonance imaging(MRI) detected T2 hyperintensity at the level of the conus medullaris and intradural flow voids in all patients. Spinal angiography confirmed the diagnosis of sacral DAVF in all cases, and complete fistula occlusion was achieved with surgical ligation in all patients. Intraoperatively, 4 patients with the midline location of the shunt point were confirmed to have FTV as the draining vein, while the other 13 patients with off-midline shunt point were confirmed to have RMV as the draining vein. The intraoperative findings were completely consistent with the preoperative assessment of the draining veins based on the location of the shunt point. CONCLUSIONS: The draining veins of sacral DAVFs are not always the FTVs, in fact, most sacral DAVFs drain via the RMV. With our simple imaging-based method, the two different types of draining veins in sacral DAVFs can be preliminarily identified before surgery.

title: Predicting acute kidney injury in type B aortic dissection: development and validation of a clinical nomogram.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) is a frequent and serious complication in patients with Type B Aortic Dissection (TBAD). Existing prediction models are mainly derived from type A or mixed cohorts and do not account for the distinct pathophysiology of TBAD. This study aimed to develop and validate a nomogram for individualized AKI risk prediction in TBAD patients. METHODS: Data were obtained from the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD) and the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV). The eICU-CRD cohort was used for model development and internal validation, while MIMIC-IV served for external validation. A three-step variable selection strategy combining Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO), univariate, and multivariate logistic regression analyses was applied. Model performance was evaluated using the Area Under the receiver operating characteristic Curve (AUC), calibration curves, and Decision Curve Analysis (DCA). RESULTS: Six independent predictors were identified: ICU length of stay, minimum glucose, minimum sodium, maximum bicarbonate, minimum creatinine, and minimum diastolic blood pressure. The nomogram showed excellent discrimination, with AUCs of 0.926 (95% CI: 0.893-0.956), 0.922 (95% CI: 0.869-0.967), and 0.921 (95% CI: 0.895-0.944) in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. Calibration analysis demonstrated good agreement, and DCA indicated clinical utility within a threshold probability range of 0-70%. CONCLUSIONS: This study developed a practical nomogram based on six readily available variables for dynamic in-hospital prediction of AKI in TBAD patients. The model may assist early risk stratification, although further prospective validation is warranted.

title: Incidence and Predictors of Symptomatic Thrombosis During Asparaginase-containing Therapy in Children With Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia: A Meta-analysis and Narrative Synthesis.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Symptomatic thrombosis is a clinically important complication of asparaginase-containing therapy in children with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), but reported incidence and predictors vary across studies. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to estimate its incidence and synthesize reported predictors. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through April 15, 2026. Eligible studies enrolled patients aged ≤21 years with ALL receiving asparaginase-containing therapy and reported extractable incidence or predictor data for overall symptomatic thrombosis or symptomatic venous thromboembolism. Proportions were pooled after logit transformation using a random-effects model. Predictor data were synthesized narratively when quantitative pooling was inappropriate. RESULTS: Twenty-three studies met the eligibility criteria; 15 studies involving 17,809 children and 655 events contributed to the incidence meta-analysis. The pooled incidence of symptomatic thrombosis was 5.6% (95% CI: 3.5%-9.0%), with substantial heterogeneity (I²=96.9%). Study-specific estimates ranged from ∼1% to 22.7%. Older age was the most consistently reported predictor; associations with inherited thrombophilia, non-O blood group, high-risk treatment status, and T-ALL phenotype were inconsistent across cohorts. CONCLUSIONS: Symptomatic thrombosis affects ∼6% of children with ALL receiving asparaginase-containing therapy, although incidence varies considerably across studies. Older age was the most reproducible risk factor, whereas evidence for other predictors remains heterogeneous.

title: Ischemic paralysis caused by internal iliac artery embolism after endovascular recanalization for lower extremity arteriosclerosis obliterans: a case report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Lower extremity paralysis is a devastating complication after endovascular therapy for lower extremity arteriosclerosis obliterans (LEAOD). Common mechanisms include ischemia-reperfusion injury, acute arterial embolism, and thrombosis. Paralysis caused by internal iliac artery embolism is exceptionally rare and may be overlooked when postoperative neurologic deficits are initially attributed to spinal or cerebral causes. CASE PRESENTATION: An 86-year-old man developed recurrent bilateral intermittent claudication 3 years after endovascular treatment for LEAOD, followed by right toe ulceration. Preoperative computed tomographic angiography showed severe multilevel stenosis and in-stent reocclusion in both lower limbs. He underwent bilateral thrombus aspiration, balloon angioplasty, and catheter-directed thrombolysis. One hour after the procedure, acute left lower limb weakness (muscle strength grade 0-1) and hypoesthesia below the mid-calf occurred. Emergency abdominal-pelvic non-contrast CT, lumbar spine MRI, brain imaging, and lower limb CTA excluded lumbar canal disease and stroke, while suggesting new internal iliac artery occlusion. Emergency thrombus aspiration and balloon angioplasty of the left internal iliac artery restored substantial patency and improved muscle strength to grade III-IV in the thigh and grade III in the leg. Because pain persisted and distal perfusion remained insufficient, femoral endarterectomy and infrapopliteal balloon angioplasty were subsequently performed. After 1 month of rehabilitation, muscle strength remained grade III, with persistent sensory impairment and assisted ambulation. CONCLUSIONS: Internal iliac artery embolism is a rare but clinically important cause of ischemic paralysis after peripheral endovascular intervention. In patients with extensive multilevel occlusive disease, preoperative assessment of internal iliac collateral perfusion and cautious staged procedural planning may reduce risk. Sudden postoperative limb paralysis should prompt urgent spinal and vascular imaging, followed by timely revascularization when ischemia is suspected.

title: Progress on the related mechanisms of vascular calcification in autogenous arteriovenous fistula in hemodialysis patients.
abstract: Autologous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred vascular access for end-stage renal disease patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis as a replacement therapy. As the duration of dialysis increases, the risk of vascular access-related complications such as AVF stenosis, thrombosis, vascular calcification (VC), and aneurysm formation gradually rises. Among these, VC has been proven to be independently associated with the occurrence and mortality of cardiovascular diseases in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). VC in the AVF of dialysis patients can lead to AVF failure, severely limiting its usability and increasing the risk of mortality among dialysis patients. Unlike previous reviews that predominantly focused on isolated mechanisms such as mineral metabolism or arterial calcification, this narrative review innovatively integrates the crosstalk among hemodynamic stress, inflammation, oxidative stress, deficiency of endogenous calcification inhibitors and pathological matrix remodeling, thereby providing a multidimensional perspective on AVF-VC. This review reframes the current understanding of AVF-VC, shifting it from a generalized complication of CKD-mineral and bone disorder to a distinct, fistula-specific pathological entity. This conceptual advancement offers a theoretical foundation for developing precision intervention strategies tailored to the unique microenvironment of the AVF.

title: Comparison of different interventions for promoting the maturation of autogenous arteriovenous fistula: A systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Autogenous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred access for patients undergoing hemodialysis. This study sought to identify the optimal intervention for promoting the maturation of AVFs through a network meta-analysis (NMA). METHODS: Cochrane Library, Embase, PubMed, and Web of Science databases were searched by computer for publications up to May 12, 2025, utilizing primary terms such as "arteriovenous fistula" and "maturation." Risk of bias was assessed utilizing the tool from the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews. Funnel plots and Egger's test were used to assess publication bias. Primary outcomes were the ultrasonographic and clinical maturation of AVFs. The secondary outcome was the vein diameter. An NMA was conducted employing a Bayesian random-effects or fixed-effects model. Mean differences (MD) and relative risks (RR) with 95% credible intervals (CrI) were calculated. Surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) values were utilized to rank different interventions. Analyses were performed using R 4.3.2. RESULTS: Finally, 11 RCTs involving 1202 patients were included. The studies encompassed a total of 5 interventions, namely isometric exercise (ISOM), isotonic exercise (ISOT), ISOM+ISOT, far infrared (FIR) therapy, and balloon-assisted maturation (BAM). The NMA revealed that compared with conventional care, ISOM ranked first in improving clinical maturation (RR = 1.4, 95% CrI: 1.2, 1.7, SUCRA = 98.07%) and ultrasonographic maturation (RR = 1.5, 95% CrI: 1.2, 1.8, SUCRA = 99.88%). ISOM+ISOT ranked first in increasing the diameter of the outflow vein (MD = 0.84, 95% CrI: 0.68, 1.0, SUCRA = 87.24%). CONCLUSION: n This study suggests that, among the evaluated interventions, ISOM has the highest probability of improving clinical maturation of AVFs based on moderate-certainty evidence, and evidence supporting its effect on ultrasonographic maturation is tentative given the limited sample size ( = 340). ISOM + ISOT demonstrated the greatest likelihood of effectively increasing vein diameter. These findings are probabilistic and require individualized application.

title: Predictive Value of Intraoperative Transcranial Doppler Hemodynamic Monitoring for Cerebral Hyperperfusion Syndrome After Carotid Artery Stenting.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cerebral hyperperfusion syndrome (CHS) is a potentially serious complication following carotid artery stenting (CAS). Conventional risk assessment methods may not adequately capture rapid intraoperative hemodynamic changes. Real-time transcranial Doppler (TCD) monitoring may provide valuable information for the early identification of patients at risk of CHS. AIMS: To investigate the predictive value of intraoperative real-time hemodynamic monitoring using TCD ultrasonography for CHS following CAS. METHODS: A total of 600 patients who underwent CAS were included. Factors associated with CHS were analyzed, and the predictive performance and clinical utility of TCD parameters measured at the T1 time point were evaluated. RESULTS: Factors associated with CHS following CAS were identified. The combined use of TCD parameters at the T1 time point demonstrated high predictive value and substantial net clinical benefit. CONCLUSION: TCD parameters measured at the T1 time point may be useful for predicting CHS following CAS and guiding clinical decision-making.

title: Retinal Microvascular Abnormalities, White Matter Injury, and Cognitive Impairment in Carotid Stenosis or Occlusion.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe carotid artery stenosis or occlusion (CASO) is associated with white matter injury and cognitive impairment, but markers of accompanying microvascular dysfunction remain incompletely characterized. We investigated the relationships among retinal microvascular abnormalities on optical coherence tomography angiography, white matter hyperintensities (WMH), and cognitive impairment in severe unilateral CASO. METHODS: In this multicenter cross-sectional study, 860 participants were included: 566 patients with severe unilateral CASO without acute cerebral infarction and 294 control participants with similar age and sex distributions. All participants underwent multimodal imaging, including automated WMH segmentation on brain magnetic resonance imaging and macular optical coherence tomography angiography. Cognitive function was assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment. RESULTS: P Compared with controls, patients with CASO showed lower vessel length density across retinal layers and greater WMH burden. Within the group with CASO, the retina ipsilateral to the stenosis showed lower vessel length density and greater vessel dilation, paralleling the greater burden of deep WMH in the ipsilateral hemisphere (all adjusted<0.05). Retinal microvascular abnormalities and greater WMH burden were both associated with worse concurrent cognitive performance. Adding optical coherence tomography angiography metrics to clinical and WMH-based models provided modest additional discrimination for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment in internal cross-validation, increasing the area under the curve from 0.652 to 0.695 (Δarea under the curve, 0.043 [95% CI, 0.021-0.064]). CONCLUSIONS: In severe unilateral CASO, retinal microvascular abnormalities were associated with ipsilateral white matter injury and lower cognitive performance. Optical coherence tomography angiographymetrics provided modest complementary discriminatory information beyond conventional clinical variables and WMH for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment, although external validation is required. abstract: BACKGROUND: Aortic dissection (AD) is a lethal cardiovascular emergency with a complex and underexplored genetic basis. METHODS: We performed whole-genome sequencing on 151 patients with sporadic Stanford type B AD and 965 healthy controls in a Chinese population as a discovery phase analysis to assess both common and rare variants. To pinpoint functional candidates, we integrated epigenomic profiles and single-cell transcriptomes from human aortic tissues. RESULTS: HLA-A HLA-DQA2 COG5 TPM4 Whole-genome sequencing analysis identified 21 candidate common loci and 2 low-frequency variants associated with AD in this discovery cohort. Two candidate common variants in the human leukocyte antigen region (rs9260945 nearand rs9276409 within) showed strong associations and colocalized with regulatory elements in aortic and immune cells, indicating immune-mediated vascular pathology. A low-frequency missense variant in thegene (rs1203229795, effect allele frequency=0.019) emerged as an independent AD risk factor, likely affecting extracellular matrix glycosylation. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis of AD-associated variants in human aortic tissues demonstrated enhanced interactions among fibroblasts, vascular smooth muscle cells, and macrophages, supporting their roles in AD pathogenesis. Integrated gene-based and expression analyses further highlighted, a marker of vascular smooth muscle cell dedifferentiation, as a putative susceptibility gene in AD. CONCLUSIONS: COG5 This multiomics investigation expands the genetic landscape of sporadic AD in Chinese individuals, revealing immune-related human leukocyte antigen loci and a functionally supported candidatevariant. Our findings offer new insights into AD pathogenesis and identify candidate targets for future diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

title: Impact of Perioperative Buyang Huanwu-Based Traditional Chinese Medicine Intervention on Postoperative Venous Thromboembolism, Coagulation Markers and Systemic Inflammation: A Propensity Score-Weighted Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to (1) evaluate, in a propensity-score-weighted retrospective cohort, the effectiveness and safety of a standardised perioperative Buyang Huanwu-based traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) decoction combined with standard low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) prophylaxis on the 30-day incidence of symptomatic and asymptomatic venous thromboembolism (VTE), (2) characterise the longitudinal trajectories of coagulation (D-dimer, fibrinogen) and inflammatory (C-reactive protein [CRP]) biomarkers and (3) quantify the net clinical benefit of this integrative approach. METHODS: n n We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 1847 adult patients undergoing major general-surgical or gynaecological procedures between January 2020 and December 2024 at a tertiary integrative-medicine centre. Patients receiving a standardised perioperative TCM decoction based on the modified Buyang Huanwu Tang in addition to standard LMWH prophylaxis (= 892) were compared with patients receiving standard prophylaxis alone (= 955). The TCM decoction comprised seven herbal components dispensed at fixed daily doses (Huangqi, 60 g; Danggui, 9 g; Chishao, 6 g; Chuanxiong, 6 g; Honghua, 3 g; Taoren, 6 g; Dilong, 9 g) supplemented with 15 g of Danshen; granules were prepared as a single-batch good manufacturing practice-certified concentrated formulation, with the principal bioactive markers astragaloside IV, ferulic acid, paeoniflorin and salvianolic acid B quantified by high-performance liquid chromatography and required to fall within ±10% of the label content to ensure dose standardisation. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was used to balance baseline characteristics. The primary outcome was 30-day VTE confirmed by duplex ultrasonography or computed tomography pulmonary angiography, with symptomatic and asymptomatic events recorded separately. Secondary outcomes included major bleeding, length of stay, patient-reported pain and 90-day all-cause mortality. Linear mixed-effects models were used to analyse longitudinal trajectories of D-dimer, fibrinogen and CRP measured at baseline and on postoperative days 1, 3 and 7. RESULTS: p p p p p After IPTW adjustment, TCM intervention was associated with significantly reduced 30-day VTE incidence (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.58, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.41-0.82,= 0.002), with consistent protection observed for both symptomatic VTE (HR: 0.55, 95% CI: 0.34-0.89) and ultrasound-detected asymptomatic distal deep-vein thrombosis (HR: 0.61, 95% CI: 0.39-0.94). Landmark analysis revealed sustained protection during both hospitalisation (HR: 0.52, 95% CI: 0.33-0.81) and the post-discharge period (HR: 0.67, 95% CI: 0.42-0.93). Linear mixed-effects modelling demonstrated significant group-by-time interactions for D-dimer (< 0.001) and CRP (= 0.003), indicating accelerated biomarker clearance in the TCM group: 42% faster D-dimer resolution and 38% faster CRP normalisation than in controls. No significant difference was observed for major bleeding (2.1% vs 2.4%,= 0.68) or 90-day all-cause mortality (1.6% vs 2.0%,= 0.51). Decision-curve analysis confirmed superior net clinical benefit across the clinically relevant threshold-probability range. CONCLUSION: Perioperative Buyang Huanwu-based TCM combined with standard LMWH prophylaxis significantly reduces postoperative VTE risk - for both symptomatic and ultrasound-detected asymptomatic events - through accelerated resolution of coagulation and inflammatory cascades, without increasing bleeding or 90-day all-cause mortality. These findings support the integration of standardised TCM into enhanced-recovery-after-surgery protocols, particularly for moderate- to high-risk surgical patients in whom anticoagulation intensification may be contraindicated.

title: A meta-analysis of transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt with or without embolization for esophageal and gastric variceal bleeding in decompensated liver cirrhosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate whether transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) combined with embolization could further improve efficacy for patients with decompensated liver cirrhosis complicated with esophageal and gastric variceal bleeding. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and Cochrane Library, for all relevant randomized controlled trials and cohort studies up to March 2025. Statistical results were evaluated using risk ratios and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: A total of 14 studies involving 3079 patients were included. The statistical results showed that the rebleeding rate in the TIPS combined with embolization group was lower than that in the TIPS alone group (risk ratios = 0.67; 95% CI = 0.57-0.79; P  < 0.001), and the same result was observed only in the subgroup of patients with gastric variceal bleeding (risk ratios = 0.50; 95% CI = 0.34-0.74; P  < 0.001). There was no significant difference between the groups in patients with isolated esophageal variceal bleeding (risk ratios = 0.83; 95% CI = 0.51-1.35; P  = 0.46). In addition, the incidence of hepatic encephalopathy in the TIPS combined with embolization group was also lower than that in the TIPS alone group (risk ratios = 0.82; 95% CI = 0.73-0.91; P  < 0.001), but there was no significant difference in survival rate (risk ratios = 1.00; 95% CI = 0.97-1.03; P  = 0.94). CONCLUSION: Compared with TIPS alone, the combined treatment showed a trend toward lower rebleeding and hepatic encephalopathy, yet survival appeared similar between the two groups.

title: Combined antegrade and retrograde transarterial approaches for embolization of a traumatic carotid‑cavernous fistula with concomitant middle meningeal arteriovenous fistula.
abstract: Endovascular treatment (EVT) is a useful modality for traumatic carotid‑cavernous fistulas (CCFs); in rare cases, combined antegrade and retrograde transarterial approaches may be applied for embolization of the fistula with concomitant internal carotid artery (ICA) sacrifice and preservation of the ophthalmic artery (OphA). A 62‑year‑old female patient sustained a motor vehicle accident and developed proptosis, chemosis, and congestion in her right eye, while no abnormalities in ocular motility or visual acuity were noted. Computed tomography angiography confirmed the CCF. Under general anesthesia, digital subtraction angiography revealed a right CCF supplied antegradely by the ICA and retrogradely by the posterior communicating artery (PcomA). A left middle meningeal arteriovenous fistula was identified. Access to the basilar artery was established. A microcatheter was retrogradely navigated via the PcomA to reach the proximal ICA across the fistula. Then, another microcatheter was advanced into the cavernous sinus via an antegrade ICA approach. Subsequently, combined antegrade and retrograde transarterial coiling with ICA sacrifice for the CCF was successfully performed. During coiling, the patency of the OphA was monitored through the PcomA microcatheter. Afterwards, the middle meningeal arteriovenous fistula was embolized. At the 1‑month follow‑up, her right eye redness and swelling resolved, and at the 3‑month follow‑up, she had recovered well and returned to her normal status. Therefore, when embolizing the CCF with ICA sacrifice, if the PcomA is well‑developed, the combined antegrade and retrograde transarterial approaches can be used, which may facilitate the obliteration of the CCF and preservation of the OphA.

title: A thoracic SMARCA4-deficient undifferentiated tumor: A case report.
abstract: Thoracic SWI/SNF-related BAF chromatin remodeling complex subunit ATPase 4 (SMARCA4)-deficient undifferentiated tumor (SMARCA4-UT) is a newly recognized, high-grade malignant neoplasm that is rare in clinical practice. There is no standardized or clearly defined treatment protocol for SMARCA4-UT in clinical guidelines. The current study reports the case of a 54-year-old male patient who presented with a 2-month history of an intermittent productive cough. Bronchoscopy demonstrated a neoplasm in the anterior segment of the right upper lobe bronchus, which almost obstructed the lumen, with a hypervascular surface, suggestive of a right upper lobe carcinoma. Histopathological examination confirmed a poorly differentiated carcinoma. Immunohistochemical analysis demonstrated a SMARCA4 gene mutation in exon 4, classifying the tumor as SMARCA4-deficient undifferentiated lung carcinoma. The patient developed superior vena cava syndrome (SVCS), requiring emergent percutaneous stent placement. Treatment also included computed tomography-guided cryoablation and radiofrequency ablation (RFA), alongside targeted molecular therapy with crizotinib. Despite aggressive multimodal therapy, the patient succumbed to tumor thrombosis at 1 month post-treatment. Overall, SMARCA4-UT is rare and diagnostically challenging, lacking standardized treatment guidelines. In clinical practice, cryoablation with argon-helium and RFA may provide palliative benefits by alleviating tumor burden and improving quality of life. Endovascular intervention provides a rapid and effective approach to alleviate tumor-induced SVCS. However, subsequent anticoagulation and antineoplastic therapies require further investigation to determine their efficacy in the management of such cases.

title: Single-stage hybrid repair of extensive aortic dissection with traumatic diaphragmatic hernia.
abstract: We report a rare case of a 70-year-old male patient who developed a left diaphragmatic hernia combined with extensive aortic dissection and exhibited signs of lower limb ischemia following a motor vehicle accident. An urgent, single-stage surgical intervention was performed, consisting of endovascular aortic repair first to stabilize circulation, followed by diaphragmatic repair. The patient recovered smoothly postoperatively, with no abnormalities observed at 1-month and 6-month follow-ups. This case highlights the necessity of accurate diagnosis and multidisciplinary team collaboration in emergency thoracoabdominal trauma.

title: SHR-2004, a Humanized Monoclonal Antibody Targeting Factor XI, for Preventing Venous Thromboembolism After Ovarian Cancer Surgery: A Randomized, Active-Controlled Phase 2 Study.
abstract: This multicenter, randomized, open-label, exploratory Phase 2 trial assessed SHR-2004, an anti-FXI antibody, for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prevention in patients undergoing ovarian cancer surgery-a population at particularly high thrombotic risk conducted at 25 sites in China. Patients with newly diagnosed Stage III-IV or recurrent ovarian cancer scheduled for surgery were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive subcutaneous SHR-2004 (180 mg on Day 1 and 120 mg on Day 15) or enoxaparin-rivaroxaban (subcutaneous enoxaparin 40 mg once daily during hospitalization, followed by oral rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily after discharge until Day 28). The primary efficacy outcome was the composite of VTE events within 28 days. The primary safety outcome was major bleeding (MB) or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding (CRNMB) from first dose to 28 days. Between February 19, 2024 and September 17, 2024, 198 patients received assigned treatment (90 with SHR-2004, 108 with enoxaparin-rivaroxaban) and were included in the safety analysis. Among 181 patients who completed protocol-mandated ultrasonography, VTE occurred in 11 (12.6%) patients in the SHR-2004 group and 19 (20.2%) in the enoxaparin-rivaroxaban group (difference -8.4%, 95% CI -19.9 to 3.1) by Day 28. MB/CRNMB rates were similar between groups (SHR-2004: 2/90 [2.2%]; enoxaparin-rivaroxaban: 2/108 [1.9%]). In this study, SHR-2004 showed comparable efficacy to enoxaparin-rivaroxaban for preventing postoperative VTE in patients undergoing ovarian cancer surgery, with a similar low risk of MB or CRNMB. The twice-monthly dosing schedule offers a potential advantage over daily anticoagulation, supporting further investigation in adequately powered Phase 3 trials. title: Segmental point obliteration technique for nerve-sparing endovenous laser ablation of the below-knee great saphenous vein.
abstract: Endovenous thermal ablation of the below-knee great saphenous vein (GSV) risks saphenous nerve injury because the vein and nerve lie in close apposition. We propose the segmental point obliteration technique, which delivers intermittent point-by-point laser pulses (6 W, ≈1 mm) instead of continuous pullback, with an interval of 1 to 2 seconds between pulses. In 13 patients (19 limbs) followed for 1 month, no paresthesia occurred, and complete occlusion was achieved in all limbs. Segmental point obliteration technique appears feasible for nerve-sparing below-knee GSV ablation, although more comparative longer-term studies are needed to determine its efficacy and overall role in below-knee GSV treatment.

title: The Imaging Compass: Navigating Reperfusion in Acute Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: The management of acute ischemic stroke has shifted from rigid time-based protocols to imaging-driven, tissue-based reperfusion strategies. Non-contrast CT and CT angiography remain the indispensable frontline for rapid triage, particularly in community and low-resource settings. However, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides unique biological information that complements CT-based assessment: Diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) detects cellular ischemia within minutes without contrast; DWI-fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) mismatch serves as a tissue clock for unknown-onset stroke; susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) aids thrombus characterization; and MRI resolves the posterior fossa without beam-hardening artifact. Low-field portable MRI further extends these capabilities to the bedside where conventional scanners are unavailable. This review examines four convergent trends within this transition: expanding thrombectomy to large-core infarction, extending thrombolysis through tissue-based selection, advancing recanalization in posterior-circulation stroke while defining boundaries for medium- and distal-vessel occlusions, and simplifying imaging workflows through fast MRI protocols, quantitative CT biomarkers, and artificial intelligence (AI). Landmark trials have established that treatment benefit is determined by tissue viability rather than clock time, while recent negative trials define critical boundaries beyond which intervention may cause harm. We critically appraise how CT and MRI are integrated hierarchically across these scenarios, and how emerging fast MRI and quantitative biomarkers may reshape future selection paradigms. title: Successful endovascular management of popliteal artery adventitial cystic disease with expanded polytetrafluoroethylene stent graft reinforced with interwoven nitinol stent.
abstract: Popliteal adventitial cystic disease has traditionally been treated with open surgery of cyst excision, patch repair of artery, or interposition graft. Endovascular angioplasty or stenting has demonstrated poor mid- to long-term results because high-viscosity tension of the adventitial cyst continues to exert extrinsic compression, resulting in early elastic recoil and disease recurrence. To our knowledge, this is the first report in the literature of an effective endovascular strategy using a popliteal stent graft reinforced with an interwoven nitinol stent to treat popliteal cysts, with favorable short- and mid-term outcome. Antiplatelet therapy should be continued, and patient should undergo regular clinical and duplex surveillance to ensure popliteal artery patency.

title: Key factors for predicting outcomes one year after Meso-Rex bypass surgery and optimizing the surgical plan in children with extrahepatic portal vein obstruction.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To analyze the factors for predicting 1-year outcomes and optimize surgical planning for Meso-Rex bypass (MRB) in children with extrahepatic portal vein obstruction (EHPVO). MATERIALS AND METHODS: From October 2014 to July 2024, children with EHPVO after MRB were retrospectively analyzed. The number of MRB, the type of bypass vessel, and the position of the lower anastomosis were collected. Predictive variables include the diameter of the connection between the left and right portal veins, the Rex vein (RV) diameter, the number of RV branches, the diameter of the thickest RV branch, and the bypass-to-superior mesenteric vein (SMV) angle, which were measured by Contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) one week after MRB. The upper and lower anastomotic stenosis were diagnosed by Ultrasound and CECT one year after MRB. RESULTS: A total of 153 children (median age 72 months, 87 males) were included in this study. Univariate factors include the number of MRBs, the type of bypass vessel, and CECT variables (except the diameter of the thickest RV branch). Numbers of MRB and RV branches were retained in the final model for upper anastomotic stenosis. The combination of MRB > 1 and RV branches ≤ 4 predicts it post-MRB with 75% sensitivity, 86.4% specificity, and an area under the receiver operator characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.832. The bypass-to-SMV angle ≤ 110° predicts lower anastomotic stenosis after MRB with 90% sensitivity, 73.39% specificity, and AUC 0.847. CONCLUSIONS: Associated factors are useful for early postoperative risk stratification. Moreover, the type of bypass vessel and the bypass-to-SMV angle could be used to inform future surgical technique refinement. KEY POINTS: QuestionWhich factors predict 1-year outcomes and optimize surgical planning for MRB in children with EHPVO? FindingsAssociated factors include bypass-to-SMV angle, number of MRB, RV branches and diameter, left-right portal vein connection diameter, and type of bypass vessel. Clinical RelevanceAssociated factors are useful for early postoperative risk stratification. Moreover, the internal jugular vein as the bridge vessel and the bypass-to-SMV angle > 110° could be used to optimize the surgical plan for a better outcome.

title: Proteomic insights of peripheral artery disease across the glycemic spectrum: a prospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) risk varies substantially across glycemic states, but glycemic status-specific proteomic features of PAD remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to provide comprehensive proteomic insights into PAD risk across the glycemic spectrum. METHODS: We included 43,875 UK Biobank participants, categorized into normoglycemia, prediabetes, and type 2 diabetes (T2D). Associations between 2920 plasma proteins and PAD were assessed using Cox regression models. PAD-related proteins underwent pathway enrichment and protein-protein interaction (PPI) analyses, and protein predictors were selected via least absolute shrinkage and selection operator models. The differential expression-sliding window analysis identified proteomic changes across the glycemic continuum. RESULTS: We identified 558 proteins associated with PAD risks, and those proteins were predominantly involved in pathways related to immune system regulation, inflammatory processes, and vascular remodeling. Two major PPI networks were identified, centered on tumor necrosis factor in normoglycemic participants and T-cell surface glycoprotein CD4 in those with T2D. The integration of protein predictors or derived protein risk scores into the clinical model significantly improved PAD prediction performance, achieving a maximum C-index of 0.834. Two proteomic peaks were revealed at glycated hemoglobin levels of 37 and 42 mmol/mol (5.5% and 6.0%), at which 11 and 4 proteins, respectively, showed potential causal associations with PAD. CONCLUSION: This study revealed glycemic state-specific proteomic features of PAD risk. These findings suggest the involvement of innate immunity in normoglycemia, and adaptive immune dysregulation with chronic inflammation in T2D. Integrating proteomic data also improved PAD risk prediction. Further validation is warranted.

title: Omega-3 fatty acids, specialized pro-resolving mediators, and depression: A mechanistic meta-analysis of precursors and clinical implications.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (n-3 PUFAs), especially eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), exhibit adjunctive antidepressant efficacy despite negligible detectable levels in the brain. Emerging evidence implicates specialized pro‑resolving mediators (SPMs); bioactive n-3 PUFA metabolites offer a coherent pathway by actively resolving inflammation, enhancing tissue repair, and supporting neuronal function. To test whether n‑3 PUFA supplementation activates pro‑resolving biology in humans, this meta‑analysis quantified effects on circulating SPM precursors. METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, GOED, and the Cochrane Library (up to May 18, 2026) to identify RCTs examining the impact of n-3 PUFAs supplementation on circulating SPM precursors 18-hydroxyeicosapentaenoic acid (18-HEPE) and 17-hydroxydocosahexaenoic acid (17-HDHA). Meta-analysis was performed using Review Manager 5.4.1 with random-effects models. RESULTS: Eleven RCTs, comprising 810 participants, were included. N-3 PUFAs supplementation significantly and robustly increased the concentrations of both circulating SPM precursors: 18-HEPE (SMD = 1.05, 95% CI 0.54-1.55, Z = 4.08, P = 0.0001) and 17-HDHA (SMD = 0.69, 95% CI 0.19-1.18, Z = 2.72, P = 0.006). Importantly, subgroup analyses revealed that this increase was selectively amplified in patient populations characterized by a significant inflammatory, metabolic, and oxidative burden, including peripheral artery disease (PAD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), MDD with comorbid obesity, and pregnancy, but was negligible in healthy infants. CONCLUSION: N-3 PUFA supplementation significantly increased circulating 18-HEPE and 17-HDHA, indicating greater availability of upstream EPA- and DHA-derived SPM precursors across mixed human populations. However, whether these precursor changes translate into increased downstream SPM production or clinical antidepressant effects remains uncertain and requires dedicated trials in MDD populations. title: Open- versus closed-cell stents in transfemoral carotid artery stenting for carotid bifurcation disease: a target trial emulation.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The comparative association of open-cell stent (OCS) and closed-cell stent (CCS) design with outcomes after protected transfemoral carotid artery stenting, particularly long-term patency, remains uncertain. This study compared OCSs and CCSs in patients with carotid bifurcation disease. METHODS: We retrospectively emulated a target trial using data from three centers. Consecutive patients who underwent transfemoral carotid artery stenting with embolic protection devices for atherosclerotic carotid bifurcation lesions were included and classified according to stent design. Stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting was used to balance baseline covariates. Periprocedural outcomes were assessed within 30 days. Follow-up outcomes included in-stent restenosis (ISR), severe ISR, symptomatic ISR, recurrent ipsilateral ischemic events (stroke or transient ischemic attack), and target-vessel revascularization. RESULTS: Among 1024 patients, 524 (51.2%) were symptomatic and 500 (48.8%) were asymptomatic; 577 received OCSs and 447 received CCSs. Median follow-up was 26.0 months (interquartile range, 19.4-32.4 months). After inverse probability of treatment weighting, baseline covariates were well balanced. Periprocedural adverse events did not differ significantly between groups. During follow-up, CCS use was associated with higher risks of ISR (hazard ratio [HR], 1.66; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.19-2.31; P = .003), severe ISR (HR, 1.61; 95% CI, 1.06-2.45; P = .026), symptomatic ISR (HR, 2.03; 95% CI, 1.20-3.45; P = .008), and recurrent transient ischemic attack (HR, 3.06; 95% CI, 1.24-7.55; P = .015). Any ISR and severe ISR were strongly associated with recurrent ipsilateral ischemic events (both P < .001). CCS use appeared more strongly associated with ISR in symptomatic patients, without significant interaction by symptom status (P for interaction = .206). Sensitivity analyses were concordant with the primary results. CONCLUSIONS: OCSs were associated with a lower hazard of restenosis and no material difference in periprocedural outcomes compared with CCSs. These findings support preferential consideration of OCSs at the carotid bifurcation for long-term patency, whereas CCSs may retain a theoretical advantage in unstable plaques requiring denser plaque coverage.

title: Interventional Therapy for Hepatic Hydatidosis with Cavernous Transformation of Portal Vein.
abstract: A 56-year-old female suffered from recurrent esophagogastric varices bleeding for 2 years due to cavernous transformation of the portal vein caused by hepatic hydatidosis. Multiple esophageal variceal ligations failed to prevent rebleeding. Transmesenteric vein extrahepatic portosystemic shunt was performed to decrease portal pressure gradient and prevent rebleeding.

title: Rethinking IVC Filter Thrombosis Diagnosis: How Stratified Ultrasound Guidance Reshapes Endovascular Practice.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To develop and evaluate a precise, ultrasound-based stratification method for diagnosing thrombus within inferior vena cava (IVC) filters, aiming to optimize diagnostic accuracy and guide clinical decision-making regarding filter management. METHODS: This single-center study, conducted at the Emergency Orthopedics and Trauma Center of Shanghai Sixth People's Hospital, enrolled 323 patients from June 2023 to June 2025 who had undergone IVC filter placement and were suspected of filter-related thrombosis. Thrombus presence and characteristics within and around the filter were assessed using conventional ultrasound (grayscale and color Doppler) and contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS). RESULTS: Based on the integrated ultrasound findings, patients were stratified into distinct management pathways: Class 0 (no thrombus) was detected in 258 cases, allowing for straightforward clinical planning. Class I/II thrombi (small, low-risk) were identified in 30 patients, enabling direct and successful filter retrieval. Class IIIa thrombi (larger, manageable) were found in 9 patients; CEUS guidance permitted careful intraoperative removal. The remaining 26 patients with Class IIIb thrombi (extensive, high-risk) received tailored treatments (eg, thrombolysis treatment, catheter placement) prior to subsequent filter removal. All filters were successfully retrieved, with surgical specimens confirming the ultrasound diagnoses. CONCLUSIONS: A stratified diagnostic approach using conventional and CEUS provides a reliable, noninvasive means to assess IVC filter thrombi. This method streamlines the diagnostic process, avoids unnecessary CEUS in clear cases, and delivers critical information for precise clinical decision-making in complex scenarios. By facilitating appropriate and individualized management plans, this approach can potentially improve patient outcomes and optimize filter retrieval workflows in emergency and trauma settings.

title: Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Risk for Thromboembolic Complication Among Patients With Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and thromboembolic events among women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study with propensity score matching. SETTING: Multicenter electronic health record database (TriNetX US Collaborative Network). POPULATION: Women aged 18-45 years with a diagnosis of PCOS between 2012 and 2021. METHODS: Women with PCOS were stratified according to subsequent diagnosis of OSA and matched 1:1 with PCOS patients without OSA using propensity scores. Incident pulmonary embolism (PE) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) occurring after a 1-year reference period were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Incident pulmonary embolism and venous thromboembolism. RESULTS: After propensity score matching, 20 052 women were included (10 026 per group). All analyses were conducted within this propensity score-matched cohort. PE incidence was higher among women with OSA compared with those without OSA (2.88 vs. 1.48 per 1000 person-years; absolute difference 1.40 per 1000 person-years; incidence rate ratio [IRR] 1.94, 95% CI 1.49-2.53; hazard ratio [HR] 1.95, 95% CI 1.50-2.54). VTE incidence was also increased (3.74 vs. 2.87 per 1000 person-years; absolute difference 0.87 per 1000 person-years; IRR 1.30, 95% CI 1.06-1.60; HR 1.32, 95% CI 1.07-1.61). These associations persisted across clinically relevant subgroups and increased over long-term follow-up. CONCLUSION: Among women with PCOS, comorbid OSA is associated with an increased risk of thromboembolic events, particularly pulmonary embolism. These findings support consideration of OSA screening and enhanced thromboembolic risk assessment in women with PCOS.

title: Diagnosis and Treatment Strategies for Femoral Vein Extramembranous Cysts: A Case Analysis and Literature Review.
abstract: IntroductionFemoral vein adventitial cystic disease is an exceedingly rare vascular disorder characterized by mucin-filled cysts within the venous wall, leading to potential luminal obstruction and clinical symptoms. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges and management of this uncommon condition.Case PresentationA 58-year-old male presented with a 2-month history of progressive left lower extremity swelling and discomfort. Physical examination revealed pitting edema along the calf. Duplex ultrasound demonstrated a hypoechoic cystic lesion compressing the femoral vein. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) confirmed a 3.1 cm × 1.4 cm × 2.1 cm cystic mass within the adventitial layer of the femoral vein, with partial luminal stenosis. No evidence of deep vein thrombosis or malignancy was observed.Intervention and OutcomeSurgical exploration via groin incision identified a translucent cyst arising from the femoral vein adventitia. Complete excision was performed with venous reconstruction. Histopathology confirmed a benign adventitial cyst with mucinous content and a single-layer endothelial lining. Postoperative recovery was uneventful, with resolution of symptoms and no recurrence at 3-month follow-up.ConclusionAdventitial cysts of the femoral vein, though rare, should be considered in patients with unexplained limb swelling. Multimodal imaging is critical for differential diagnosis, and complete surgical excision remains the definitive treatment. This case underscores the importance of recognizing atypical venous pathologies to prevent misdiagnosis and ensure optimal outcomes.

title: Peripheral Artery Disease Burden in Different Development Regions: Based on GBD 2021.
abstract: BackgroundPeripheral artery disease (PAD) is a major global health problem with marked regional disparities. Updated estimates are needed to better characterize these differences and inform priority-setting in prevention and management.MethodsUsing GBD 2021 data, we estimated PAD prevalence, years of life lost (YLLs), years lived with disability (YLDs), and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) in High-income North America (HINA), the Caribbean, and Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). Outcomes were reported as counts, crude rates, and age-standardized rates (ASRs), with stratification by sex, socio-demographic index (SDI), and age. Temporal trends from 1990 to 2021 and risk factor-attributable DALYs were also assessed.ResultsFrom 1990 to 2021, PAD cases increased by 72% in HINA, 127% in the Caribbean, and 137% in SSA, while DALYs increased by 84%, 168%, and 203%, respectively. Prevalence and DALY ASRs declined slightly in HINA, increased moderately in the Caribbean, and rose more markedly in SSA. Women showed higher prevalence and YLD burden, whereas men had higher YLL and mortality. Tobacco use and high fasting plasma glucose contributed more prominently to the attributable burden in HINA and the Caribbean, whereas high systolic blood pressure and kidney dysfunction were more prominent in SSA. PAD burden increased substantially after age 60 and peaked in the oldest age groups.ConclusionPAD burden continues to rise, with SSA showing the least favorable age-standardized trends. These findings highlight substantial regional heterogeneity and may help identify priorities for earlier detection, risk-factor control, and long-term PAD management, particularly in lower-resource settings.

title: Soft robotic devices for cardiovascular medicine.
abstract: Conventional, rigid simulators and therapeutic devices for cardiovascular disease have several fundamental limitations, such as poor biomimetic fidelity, substantial surgical invasiveness and mismatch at the tissue-device interface. Soft robotic devices, with tissue-like materials, structures and functions, are emerging as promising alternatives. In this Review, by matching clinical demands to technological breakthroughs, we identify three emerging complementary frontiers in which soft robotic devices are redefining cardiovascular medicine - soft robotic simulators, such as in vitro ventricular simulators and in vivo assistive simulators; soft robotic interventional instruments, such as percutaneous instruments, endovascular continuum instruments and untethered mini-scale robots; and soft robotic implants for vascular disease, arrhythmia and heart failure. We describe the unique advantages of soft robotic devices as well as their applicable scope and technical implementation. Finally, we highlight promising technological opportunities for next-generation soft cardiac devices, evaluate the clinical maturity of existing devices and propose a translational roadmap for the coming decade. With this Review, we aim to foster further integration of soft robotics into cardiovascular medicine by identifying device solutions with translational potential to address unmet clinical needs.
